{{confuse|coherent category}}
In mathematics, a '''coherent topos''' is a [[topos]] generated by a collection of quasi-compact quasi-separated objects closed under finite products.<ref>[[Jacob Lurie]], [https://www.math.ias.edu/~lurie/278x.html Categorical Logic (278x)]. Lecture 11. Definition 6.</ref>

[[Deligne's completeness theorem]] says a coherent topos has [[enough points]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Frot |first1=Benjamin |title=Godel's Completeness Theorem and Deligne's Theorem |date=2013 |class=math.LO |eprint=1309.0389 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Deligne completeness theorem|website=[[nLab]]| url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Deligne+completeness+theorem }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Grothendieck |first1=A. |author-link=Alexander Grothendieck |chapter=Site et Topos etales d'un schema, 9. Appendice. Critère d’existence de points par P. Deligne |title=Théorie des Topos et Cohomologie Etale des Schémas |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |date=1972 |volume=270 |pages=341–365 |doi=10.1007/BFb0061323 |isbn=978-3-540-06012-3 }}</ref>
